sentence: This project manages patient data and bone marrow samples and links clinical data to research results for people with multiple myeloma.
This project studies how regions that control genes, and RNA in cartilage, may be linked to adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
This project provides shared resources that help scientists better understand how the body works in diabetes.
This project studies why people who have bariatric surgery are at higher risk of suicide, using health records and interviews.
This project tries to find out whether natural virus infections change gene therapy vectors in human hepatocytes.
This project tries to find out what the spike proteins of coronaviruses look like in different shapes when they sit in a membrane.
This project studies how gene regulation differs between heart chambers and how it relates to heart diseases.
This project studies how the immune systems of bacteria work at the molecular level.
This project studies how alternative splicing and RNA-binding proteins affect the start and progress of the autoimmune process leading to type 1 diabetes.
This project builds computational methods that use spatial transcriptomics data to study how the arrangement of cells affects patient survival and drug combinations.
This project tries to find out how adeno-associated viruses reach and stay at nuclear sites in cells.
This project uses infectious microbes to study how the actin cytoskeleton works and is controlled.
This project builds a hydrogel that delivers muscle stem cells to repair diaphragm muscle in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
This project studies how pain circuits change in animals after peripheral nerve injury leads to chronic pain.
This project tests several drugs in one platform trial for children and young adults with relapsed or refractory Ewing sarcoma.
This project brings in organ-on-a-chip technology, which uses chips lined with living human cells to copy how human organs work.
This project studies which human proteins change when HIV and hepatitis B virus infect the same cells, to find ways to cure hepatitis B.
This project studies how the flexibility of metamaterial interbody cages affects spinal fusion in vivo.
This project finds regulatory parts of the genome tied to maternal fetal diseases and builds a model to predict a person's risk of them.
This project builds tools that find which proteins bind to transcription factors and how these bindings control gene expression.
